raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year on my fields.

---

I'm 44, been doing this since I came to this village when I was married. My man works construction over in Handan most of the year, only home for holidays and the busy season. My oldest boy is at the factory. So it's mostly me in the fields, with my mother-in-law helping when her back allows, and the younger ones pitch in during harvest when school is out.

2.6 mu — that's not much land. Seven of us eating from this and whatever the menfolk send back. Most of what I grow, we eat. What's left over after we keep grain for the year, I sell at the grain station to pay for the seeds and fertilizer for next time. That's how it works.

**The wheat first.** I'll plant around the beginning of the cold dew (寒露), same as always, right after the maize comes off in early October. Everyone in the village plants that week. I buy Jimai seed from the supply shop in town — about 25 jin per mu, costs me maybe 70, 75 yuan a mu. I don't save my own seed, the yield drops too much, everyone knows that.

For fertilizer, I'll do like last year. One bag of compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 kind — covers about 2 mu for the base before planting. Then when it warms up in spring and the wheat starts standing up tall at jointing, I'll topdress urea. About half a bag per mu, maybe a little more if the wheat looks yellow. My neighbor Old Liu puts on more, close to 30 kg of urea, but his plot has better soil and he's got his son helping. I don't have that kind of cash sitting around.

Water: I'll irrigate three times. Once over winter if it's dry — last winter I skipped it because we had some snow and it cost me maybe 30 kg per mu at harvest, lesson learned. Then at jointing with the topdress, and once at heading. The well is shared, we take turns. The electricity is about 12-15 yuan per mu each time.

For bugs, I spray once for aphids in the spring if I see them on the leaves, and weed killer once in late winter. Nothing special. I usually get around 400 to 420 kg per mu — last year was 430, a decent year.

**Then the maize.** Tight, tight turnaround. Wheat off, maize in, maybe 3 or 4 days. I hire the combine and the maize planter — the fellow in the village runs both with one pass through, costs about 80 yuan per mu all in. Zhengdan 958 seed, everybody around here plants it, about 40 yuan a mu.

For maize fertilizer I do less base than wheat — maize doesn't need as much — about 20 kg per mu of compound. Then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口), about 15 kg per mu. I only irrigate maize once, usually around tasseling time if it hasn't rained enough. Summer rains do most of the work. I spray once for the borer worm.

Maize yields me around 450 to 500 kg per mu. Together with the wheat, we've got grain for the year and a bit left to sell. Not much left over after fertilizer costs, but enough.

Whole year for 2.6 mu I'll probably spend around 1,400 to 1,500 yuan on inputs and hired machines. Labor I don't count — that's my two hands.
